描述_ZN: Imitation of a Landscape in the Northern Garden" scroll, 1655, painted by Zhang Xuezeng on paper with ink brush, 93 cm in length and 41.5 cm in width.　　This painting shows a huge rocky mountain in the distance, painted with a pistachio, with ink dots applied to the mountain and the trees and moss and grass in the near distance, and a small bridge extending away. The composition is simple and distant, with endless rhythm. The name "Beiyuan" refers to the famous landscape painter Dong Yuan of the Southern Tang Dynasty during the Five Dynasties, as he was the envoy of Beiyuan. The brushwork in the painting is pale and blank, exuding the influence of Dong Qichang on the dryness and intensity of the brushwork, as well as the blandness and innocence of the painting style.　　The signature reads, "In the mid-winter of the year yiwei, the painting imitates Beiyuan like Zhang Xuezeng of the word world of Zimu." Inscriptions: "Zhang Xuezeng Seal" in white and "Zhang Erwei's" in vermilion. The year "Yiwei" is the twelfth year of the reign of Shunzhi of the Qing Dynasty (1655).　　The collection marks include those of Sun Yupeng and Pang Laishen: "Sun Yupeng Collection Seal" in vermilion, "Xiyi" in white, "Xuzhai Review" in white, and "Pang Laishen Collection Seal" in white. Pang Lai-chen Collection Seal" in vermilion.
